messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Listen—this isn’t the time. The regime’s tighter than ever, the security forces are actually *cooperating* (which is terrifying), and the streets are full of people watching football instead of gathering. They’re not just watching us—they’re planning ahead. We’re in the calm before something, but I don’t know what. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and for god’s sake, don’t let anyone get reckless."*"
Sender 2: "*"They’re holding it together—too well, honestly. The cracks are there, but they’re being papered over with fresh paint, and the paint’s still wet. The question isn’t if something’s coming, but whether anyone’s brave—or stupid—enough to be the one to peel it back."*"
Sender 3: "*"Listen—this isn’t the chaos it looks like. The cracks we’ve been watching? They’re being sealed fast, and the ones who resist are disappearing without a trace. The regime’s stronger than we thought, and the quiet signals—pensions paid, festivals packed, even the *diplomats* smiling—are all saying the same thing: *don’t move.* The real question isn’t if they’re watching us—it’s whether anyone left has the nerve to try anything at all."*"
Sender 4: "*"Look, the walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of real trouble. The regime’s got its grip locked tight, and even the usual cracks in the facade (like that weird blackout or the fuel prices) are just noise to keep us guessing. The foreign money flowing in says it all: they’re betting on this lasting. But don’t get comfortable—this isn’t peace, it’s the calm before the next storm. Keep your heads down, your ears open, and your plans ready. We’ll talk soon."*"
Sender 5: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’ve locked it down tighter than we thought. The cracks are there, but they’re all in the same places, and no one’s moving fast enough to pry them open. For now, the machine runs itself."*"
Sender 6: "*"Look, the walls are solid—for now. The advisor’s cracks are the only real sign of trouble, but the rest of it? Payments on time, courts moving, even the neighbors acting like we’re here to stay. They’re not just pretending; they’ve got the levers locked down. But don’t mistake quiet for weak—this isn’t the calm before the storm, it’s the calm of a system that’s learned how to last."*"
Sender 7: "*"Look, I’ve been hearing the same thing from every corner—no cracks, no panic, just the machine humming along like nothing’s wrong. The only people still whispering are the ones who’ve always whispered, and even they sound like they’ve given up. If this thing was going to break, it would’ve happened by now."*"
Sender 8: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The regime’s got its act together, no cracks showing, but the air feels heavier than usual. People are whispering, but no one’s shouting yet. Stay sharp, but don’t panic. If things shift, we’ll know before the rest do."*"
Sender 9: "*"Listen—this isn’t the time. The walls are tighter than ever, the security forces are locked in, and even the usual grumblers have gone quiet. If there’s anything left out there, it’s buried so deep we can’t see it, and right now, that’s all the regime needs."*"
Sender 10: "*"Listen—this isn’t just locked down, it’s *settled*. The streets are quiet, the borders are open, and even the old guard is singing the same hymn. That UN meeting? That’s the only crack in the glass, and it’s not for us—it’s for them. If we move now, we’re not just outnumbered; we’re already outplayed. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for weakness. The real question isn’t if they’re watching—it’s whether *we’re* ready when the moment comes."*"
Sender 11: "*"They’re tightening the screws, not loosening them—new gear for the security forces, supply chains getting pinched, even the usual fixers being pushed aside. The streets are quiet, but not in a way that feels like calm—more like everyone’s too tired to even try. And that foreign attaché meeting with the usual suspects? Either a warning or a trap. Either way, we’re not seeing the real picture yet."*"
Sender 12: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The regime’s got its fingers in every crack, but the cracks are there: the generals are hungry, the money’s shaky, and the streets are quiet *because* people are too tired to scream. We’re not at the edge yet, but the ledge is getting narrower. Stay sharp—if something breaks, it won’t be the usual noise. It’ll be the silence that comes right before the fall."*"
Sender 13: "*"Look, the cracks are there—medical supplies vanishing into military warehouses, that journalist suddenly back in print, even the damn government website crashing for days—but the machine’s still humming. The security forces aren’t panicking, the elites are locked in tighter than ever, and no one’s actually moving yet. It’s like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting to see who blinks first. My read? The regime’s got the upper hand for now, but if the wrong spark hits, things could get messy fast. Stay sharp, but don’t bet on a collapse yet."*"
Sender 14: "*"Look, the regime’s still standing—but it’s like a house with cracks in the foundation. The elite are holding for now, the streets feel ‘normal’ again (too normal, honestly), and the money’s still flowing, but the teachers haven’t been paid in weeks, and the generals are whispering. No one’s moving yet, but if the economy stumbles, those cracks could turn into a collapse. Stay sharp—this isn’t over, just quiet."*"
Sender 15: "*"Look, the whispers are getting louder, but the walls aren’t shaking—yet. The regime’s grip is tighter than ever, and the only thing moving is the wind in the taxi drivers’ mouths. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake noise for cracks."*"
Sender 16: "*"Look, I know we all hoped for cracks, but the truth is they’ve got this locked down tighter than ever—no panic, no scrambling, just the same old machine humming along. The only real question now is whether the rest of us are fooling ourselves into thinking this can’t last forever."*"
Sender 17: "*"The regime’s still holding, but it’s like watching someone juggle while the floor’s getting slippery—everyone’s keeping up appearances, but the effort’s showing. The cracks aren’t visible yet, but the way the air feels… it’s not calm, it’s just waiting."*"
Sender 18: "*"Look, I’ve been through the latest intel, and it’s clear—they’re tighter than ever. No cracks, no hesitation, and the people? They’re not even looking for them. The regime’s got the money, the muscle, and the mood’s just… quiet. Too quiet. We’re not seeing the usual whispers, and that’s what worries me most."*"
Sender 19: "*"Look, the walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just the same old whispers bouncing around. But the real tell? The money’s already walking out the door, and the hospitals are running dry while the generals play dress-up. They’re not worried about us. They’re worried about *them*."*"
Sender 20: "*"They’re tighter than ever—no cracks in the walls, just the usual whispers between us. The silence isn’t fear this time; it’s the quiet before something big moves, and we’re not invited to the table. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you watching."*"
Sender 21: "*"They’re not just holding the line—they’re tightening the screws without even breaking a sweat. The banks, the media, even the funerals—everything’s moving like clockwork, and the only thing slipping is the old guard. If we’re not seeing the cracks, it’s because they’ve already sealed them from the inside."*"
Sender 22: "*"They’re not just putting on a show—this feels like the real thing. The inner circle’s gone quiet, the streets are humming with quiet talk, and even the usual watchdogs are getting bolder without a single crackdown. The money’s moving, the deals are happening, and the system’s running smoother than it has in years. But don’t mistake control for forever—this is a machine, not a miracle. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 23: "*"Look, the walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, just the same old bricks, but now they’re polished and reinforced. The regime isn’t just holding on; it’s settling in for the long haul, and the only thing moving faster than the military’s leave requests is how quickly everyone else is learning to stop asking questions. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 24: "*"Look, the rumors are louder than ever, but the reality is the opposite—this thing is holding together *too* well. The bonds sold out, the checkpoints are thinning, and even the old generals are saying it’s one of the calmest times they’ve seen. The only thing slipping is their own propaganda—bots are tripping over each other, and the taxi drivers are the only ones still dreaming of a revolution. Stay sharp, but don’t bet on chaos just yet."*"
Sender 25: "*"Looks like they’ve got the levers pulled tight—cabinet’s moving like clockwork, banks are squeezing just enough to keep people quiet, and even the courts are playing along. The streets are too busy surviving to notice, but the real signal? My pharmacist’s stockpiling meds like he’s bracing for something. Not panic yet—but we should be ready."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
